correctness.rationale: The ordinary matching complex of the explicit 12-vertex 30-edge icosahedral graph has matching face vector (30,315,1400,2535,1482,125), plus augmented empty cell. Independent exact sparse integer cancellation of its boundary complex finds 2911 pivots of coefficient ±1 and leaves 65 degree-three cells and one degree-four cell; its one boundary column has 35 nonzero entries with gcd 3, proving reduced H3=Z^64⊕Z/3 and vanishing elsewhere. Independent signed antipodal-involution chain decomposition over F3 yields dimension C4=741 in each parity, (rank d4,rank d5)=(686,55) in plus and (670,70) in minus, giving H4 parity 0,1. Naturality of universal coefficients identifies H4(F3)=Tor(H3(Z),F3), so inversion is -1 on unique Z/3. Over F5, rank recomputation gives rational H3 parity 40,24 (no 5-primary torsion). Independently enumerated Aut(I) has order 120, its commutator subgroup size 60 excludes antipode, so torsion character factors through G/G′=C2 and is nontrivial. These are exact finite exhaustive computations, not mere logged verifier success. Integer units imply genuine chain homotopy equivalences; rational action is not claimed for whole G.

value.rationale: The canonical planar icosahedral graph is a natural, small example carrying exceptional 3-torsion in matching homology. Its graph antipode has a geometrically meaningful action; proving torsion is odd while most rational H3 is even identifies a genuine distinction invisible to nonequivariant Betti numbers and rules out a globally invariant torsion generator. The exact complete torsion character on Aut(I) is a mathematically motivated representation invariant, not a random finite slice.
residual_risks: No full integral G-lattice or all-isotypic rational decomposition and no general graph family theorem asserted.
